points.why: It describes the structure as a dominant strategy where each team gains by padding, but never names the commons or frames the cost as spread across everyone sharing a finite resource.
It says emails fail because padding is rational and the team that submits only what it needs loses, so no greed is required.
It recommends enforced fair-share scheduling, per-team queue caps, a public usage dashboard and rules shaped with team leads, all tied to each team's recent consumption.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects more emails and relies on changing the rules.
It never proposes adding GPUs as the fix.
